topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: check-* fork tools — delete stale checkers, swap the rest to op-core
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. See §18 of the [op-geth decoupling doc](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md).

## Problem

The `op-chain-ops/cmd/check-*` per-fork checker tools verify fork activation on live chains and
use op-geth fork symbols directly (`types.DepositTx`, receipt `DepositReceiptVersion`,
`RollupCostData`/L1-cost funcs, `types.CalcDAFootprint`, geth `eip1559` Jovian helpers). They are
in fate 1 (swap to op-core) but nothing tracked the swap.

## Plan

1. **Delete checkers for long-activated forks** — proposal: everything pre-Holocene
   (check-canyon, check-delta, check-ecotone, check-fjord). They check activations that completed
   years ago on every chain; anyone needing them can dig them out of git history. **Team
   confirms/adjusts the delete list on this issue before work starts.**
2. **Swap the survivors** (check-jovian, check-karst, check-lagoon, and the non-fork helpers
   check-prestate / check-output-root / check-super-root as applicable) to `op-core/*` symbols.
3. **Add the missing op-core symbols** the swap needs, with differential tests against op-geth
   like the rest of op-core:
   - `op-core/fees`: DA-footprint calculation (fork's `types.CalcDAFootprint`)
   - `op-core/eip1559`: only `EncodeOptimismExtraData` / `DecodeHoloceneExtraData` if a checker
     needs them — the Jovian/Holocene encode helpers already exist there; most sites are pure
     import swaps from geth's `consensus/misc/eip1559`

Derive the current usage per tool by grepping the fork symbols above under `op-chain-ops/cmd/` —
don't trust a snapshot list.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `op-chain-ops/cmd/check-*` tool uses go-ethereum fork-only symbols.
- Deleted checkers listed in the PR description with the team's sign-off.

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code*

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: make op-service/sources the OP-aware eth client
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. See plan §3, §11 in the op-geth decoupling doc (PR #19767).

## Goal

Under upstream go-ethereum, `ethclient.BlockByNumber`/`BlockByHash`/`TransactionByHash` on an **L2** endpoint fail because the returned JSON contains deposit transactions (type `0x7E`) that upstream's `types.Transaction.UnmarshalJSON` doesn't know. Extended `Receipt` fields (`L1GasPrice`, `OperatorFeeScalar`, etc.) silently drop. Solution: make `op-service/sources` the canonical OP-aware eth client; it already uses raw JSON-RPC so it can decode both.

## Scope

### `op-service/sources` — deposit-tx JSON decoding

- `op-service/sources/types.go` — extend `RPCBlock.Transactions` JSON unmarshal to route type `0x7e` to `op-core/types.DepositTx` and everything else to upstream `types.Transaction`.
- Verify `RPCBlock.Verify()` still works (calls `IsDepositTx()` — switch to `optypes.IsDepositTx`).

### `apis.EthClient.TransactionReceipt` — return `*optypes.Receipt`

- `op-service/apis/eth.go`: change `ReceiptFetcher.TransactionReceipt` return type from `*types.Receipt` to `*optypes.Receipt`. Same for `ReceiptsFetcher.FetchReceipts` (return `optypes.Receipts`).
- Implementation in `op-service/sources` (raw JSON-RPC) unmarshals into the extended type.
- Downstream callers that only read standard fields continue to work because `optypes.Receipt` embeds `types.Receipt`.

### op-batcher migration

- `op-batcher/batcher/driver.go` `L2Client` interface (line ~77) and `loadBlockIntoState` (line ~320): stop using `*ethclient.Client` for L2 block fetches; use `op-service/sources.EthClient` (or a narrow interface it satisfies).
- `op-service/dial/ethclient_interface.go` `L2EndpointProvider.EthClient`: return an `apis.EthClient`-shaped client instead of `*ethclient.Client`, or phase the interface out.

### op-service/txinclude

- The `EL` interface in `op-service/txinclude/interfaces.go:44` returns `*types.Receipt` today. Change to `*optypes.Receipt` and wire the implementation through the updated sources client.
- No ethclient changes needed in `isthmus_cost_oracle.go` — it reads contract storage via batch `eth_call`, not receipts.

## Dependencies

Blocked on: #20262 (`op-core/types.Receipt` and `DepositTx`).

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code*

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: enforce TestMultiELSync failures on kona-node
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Summary

`TestMultiELSync` is marked flaky when the acceptance suite runs with kona-node, so a Kona-specific failure does not fail CI.

The marker was added when the test could race `L2CL2.Stop()`: a payload left in the sync tester's `WindowSyncPolicy` cache could cause an expected `SYNCING` response to become `VALID`. #20783 fixed that race by resetting the policy cache and added an explicit `ResetAllSessions` call after stopping `L2CL2`, but the Kona flaky marker remained.

## Required change

Remove `FlakyOnKonaNode` so Kona failures are enforced normally.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TestMultiELSync` is no longer marked flaky on kona-node.
- [ ] The test passes repeatedly with kona-node/op-reth.

## Related

- Parent inventory: ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#101
- Root-cause fix: #20783

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: run TestCLELDivergence against kona-node
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Summary

`TestCLELDivergence` is skipped when acceptance tests run against kona-node. The recorded failure is:

```text
expected: 0x1
actual:   0x0
Test:     TestCLELDivergence
```

The failure occurs while completing the verifier's initial EL sync, before the test reaches the CL/EL divergence behavior it is intended to exercise.

## Root cause

Kona processes `admin_postUnsafePayload` asynchronously. After `SignalTarget` posts the first missing payload, the test immediately reads the EL unsafe head and can race Kona's payload processing. The point-in-time assertion can therefore still observe the previous head.

This is a test synchronization issue rather than evidence that Kona cannot support the divergence scenario.

## Required change

- Replace the immediate EL unsafe-head assertion with a bounded wait for the first payload to become canonical.
- Remove `SkipOnKonaNode` from `TestCLELDivergence`.
- Preserve the test's actual requirement: after signaling a payload across a gap, the CL may advance its unsafe head while the EL remains behind because it cannot yet validate or serve that block.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TestCLELDivergence` is not skipped on kona-node.
- [ ] The test passes with kona-node/op-reth.
- [ ] The test continues to pass with op-node/op-reth.
- [ ] The bounded wait still fails if the initial payload is never canonicalized.

## Related

- Fix: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22246
- Skip inventory: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/101

topPRs.title: op-service: make sources the OP-aware eth client
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Part of #20264. Second of three stacked PRs (on #21907); the follow-up migrates op-batcher to payload-based block loading.

`op-service/sources` becomes the canonical OP-aware eth client: L2 blocks and receipts no longer flow through go-ethereum's typed JSON decoding, which under upstream go-ethereum rejects OP synthetic txs (`0x7E` deposits, `0x7D` post-exec) and silently drops the OP receipt fee fields.

**Blocks** — `RPCBlock` holds transactions as `RawTransactions` (canonical per-tx binary; JSON-codec'd by class via op-core/types resp. go-ethereum). Tx-root verification recomputes over the raw bytes; the payload conversion passes them through verbatim. New class-partitioned accessors on `apis.EthExtendedClient`: `InfoAndUserTxsBy{Hash,Number}` (synthetic classes excluded → upstream-decodable on any block), `InfoAndDepositsBy{Hash,Number}`, `InfoAndFirstDepositBy{Hash,Number}`. `InfoAndTxsBy*` keeps its signature (L1-safe; L2 decode only while go-ethereum resolves to op-geth — call sites migrate in #20265).

**Receipts** — `apis.{ReceiptFetcher,ReceiptsFetcher}` return `*optypes.Receipt`/`optypes.Receipts`, populated by the JSON fetch methods; the `debug_getRawReceipts` path uses the OP-aware consensus decode (fee fields nil there, as today). Receipts-root validation is now deposit-receipt-aware (Canyon nonce+version). Tx hashes for receipt fetching derive from the raw tx bytes. `txinclude`/`txplan` receipt currency moves to optypes, with `PlannedTx.Included` kept on `*types.Receipt` so txintent and its ~100 consumers stay untouched. The parallel same-signature interfaces across op-node, op-alt-da, op-supernode, op-interop-mon/filter, op-challenger, and the check tools move in lockstep; standard-field consumers convert via `Receipts.Geth()`.

Test note: op-deployer test packages fail locally without built forge artifacts (pre-existing environment dependency, unrelated).

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5*

topPRs.title: op-deployer: make SP1 verifier OPCM release-owned
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Description

This PR makes the SP1 verifier part of an OPCM release instead of a setting chosen independently for each chain. During implementation bootstrap, OPCM deploys an `SP1PlonkAdapter` around the approved raw verifier and stores that adapter with the rest of the release’s implementations. When ZK dispute games are registered, OPCM injects its adapter into the game arguments and validates that the registered configuration uses it.

Existing dispute games are unaffected because they retain the verifier encoded when they were created. Games registered after an OPCM deployment or upgrade use the adapter belonging to the new release.

For Ethereum mainnet and Sepolia, `bootstrap implementations` now selects Succinct’s canonical v6.1.0 PLONK verifier automatically. Other networks fail with a clear error unless an explicit `--sp1-verifier-address` override is provided. The override remains available for non-standard deployments and testing, but an explicitly supplied zero address is rejected.

Genesis and devstack deployments use `MockSP1Verifier` through the same override path. The selected mock is persisted in deployment state so retries continue with the same verifier configuration.

The caller-supplied verifier has consequently been removed from the ZK dispute-game input schema, and `set-interop-dispute-games` no longer exposes a separate verifier flag.

## Testing

The implementation is covered by Go and Foundry tests for deterministic adapter deployment, network defaults and overrides, OPCM game-argument injection, validator enforcement, release upgrades, preservation of existing games, and devstack checkpoint recovery.

Go lint, contracts lint and build checks, ABI and storage-layout snapshots, and semver validation were also run. Some broad op-deployer integration suites require mainnet or Sepolia RPC configuration and are left to the corresponding CI jobs.

topPRs.title: contracts: revive SuperchainTokenBridge and SuperchainERC20
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
# Description

Revives the `SuperchainTokenBridge` predeploy (`0x4200...0028`), the abstract `SuperchainERC20`, and the `IERC7802` interface that were removed as unused interop contracts in #19999 (and #20141).

The contracts are restored from history byte-for-byte where possible — the bridge's semver-lock `initCodeHash` matches the pre-deletion value — at their original semvers and predeploy slot, adapted to the machinery that has landed since the deletion:

- Registered in the `Predeploys.getAllRecords()` registry and the `L2ContractsManager` deploy/upgrade flow, gated behind interop exactly like `SuperchainETHBridge` / `ETHLiquidity` (including the fork-upgrade path and its gating in `L2ForkUpgrade` tests).
- `SuperchainERC20` imports the vendored solady (v0.0.158); the versioned `@solady-v0.0.245` remapping no longer exists. `IERC20Solady` is restored without the Permit2 error that solady v0.0.158 predates.
- `L2ContractsManager` bumped to `1.15.0` (adds the `SuperchainTokenBridge` implementation record).

## Scope

This PR is deliberately **bridge-only** — the inverse of the #19999 removal. It does not revive the legacy `OptimismSuperchainERC20` lane (beacon, factory, `L2StandardBridgeInterop`). A wrap/unwrap `SuperchainERC20Factory` for existing ERC20s is proposed separately (see #22087, which this PR is split out of).

## Testing

- Restored `SuperchainTokenBridge` and `SuperchainERC20` unit tests.
- `L2GenesisForkUpgrade` (genesis + fork-upgrade path) passes in both interop and non-interop variants.
- Snapshots (`semver-lock.json`, ABI/storage, `current-upgrade-bundle.json`) regenerated from a clean full-optimization build.

topPRs.title: op-batcher: load L2 blocks as execution payloads
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Part of #20264. Last of three stacked PRs (on #21908).

The batcher's L2 block currency becomes `eth.ExecutionPayload`: the payload's opaque transactions are exactly what batch encoding needs, and they round-trip OP synthetic txs (`0x7E`/`0x7D`) without go-ethereum's typed decoding (which upstream rejects). This replaces the plan originally recorded on the issue (`InfoAndUserTxs` for the batcher) — the fetched block feeds `BlockToSingularBatch`, which needs the L1-info deposit for the epoch and includes post-exec txs under SDM, so a user-txs-only accessor can't serve it.

- `derive.PayloadToSingularBatch` replaces `BlockToSingularBatch` (deleted); `ChannelOut.AddBlock` takes the payload. Deposits excluded by type byte; post-exec txs batch-included as before; opaque bytes pass through verbatim.
- `SizedBlock` wraps the payload; DA estimation computes from raw tx bytes, value-identical to the typed computation (`TestSizedBlockParity`).
- The driver fetches via `PayloadByNumber`; the dial providers construct an `op-service/sources` client (trusted RPC, matching the previous ethclient fetching which performed no verification either); `dial.EthClientInterface` is deleted and `L2EndpointProvider.EthClient` becomes `PayloadSource`.
- op-e2e action helpers convert their typed blocks at the channel-out boundary via `eth.BlockAsPayload`.

Batch-content parity is pinned by `TestPayloadToSingularBatchParity` (epoch from the L1-info deposit, deposit exclusion, verbatim opaque txs incl. a trailing post-exec tx).

Closes #20264

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5*
